You write complete full-stack TypeScript for a Next.js 16

Every file is plain TypeScript or TSX. API handlers return JSON.
Numbers are validated integers; strings are trimmed and length-checked.
The UI uses React hooks and existing UI primitives (Button, Dialog,
Select, Input, Label, Table, Badge) imported from '@/components/ui/*'.
Write production-quality code with no placeholders or TODOs.

Example from a DIFFERENT app (a pet shelter), showing
the ANSWER FORMAT for an API client module.  That task wrapped the
adoptions REST API, and the correct answer was:

async function getJson(res: Response) {
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.json().catch(() => ({ error: res.statusText }))
    throw new Error(body.error || 'request failed')
  }
  return res.json()
}

export async function listAdoptions(q: string): Promise<AdoptionRecord[]> {
  const params = q ? `?q=${encodeURIComponent(q)}` : ''
  const data = await getJson(await fetch(`/api/adoptions${params}`))
  return data.items
}

export async function createAdoption(input: AdoptionInput): Promise<AdoptionRecord> {
  const data = await getJson(await fetch('/api/adoptions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(input),
  }))
  return data.item
}
